From 069daad4f2ae9c5c108131995529d5f02392c446 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Steffen Klassert <steffen.klassert@secunet.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Apr 2026 13:31:04 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] xfrm: Wait for RCU readers during policy netns exit

xfrm_policy_fini() frees the policy_bydst hash tables after flushing the
policy work items and deleting all policies, but it does not wait for
concurrent RCU readers to leave their read-side critical sections first.

The policy_bydst tables are published via rcu_assign_pointer() and are
looked up through rcu_dereference_check(), so netns teardown must also
wait for an RCU grace period before freeing the table memory.

Fix this by adding synchronize_rcu() before freeing the policy hash tables.

Fixes: e1e551bc5630 ("xfrm: policy: prepare policy_bydst hash for rcu lookups")
Signed-off-by: Steffen Klassert <steffen.klassert@secunet.com>
Reviewed-by: Florian Westphal <fw@strlen.de>

diff --git a/net/xfrm/xfrm_policy.c b/net/xfrm/xfrm_policy.c
index 362939aa56cf..8f0188e763c7 100644
--- a/net/xfrm/xfrm_policy.c
+++ b/net/xfrm/xfrm_policy.c
@@ -4290,6 +4290,8 @@ static void xfrm_policy_fini(struct net *net)
 #endif
 	xfrm_policy_flush(net, XFRM_POLICY_TYPE_MAIN, false);
 
+	synchronize_rcu();
+
 	WARN_ON(!list_empty(&net->xfrm.policy_all));
 
 	for (dir = 0; dir < XFRM_POLICY_MAX; dir++) {
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Patch

### Modifications in Each File

1. **`net/xfrm/xfrm_policy.c`** (line 4290)
   - **Added:** A call to `synchronize_rcu()` immediately after `xfrm_policy_flush()` and before the subsequent code that frees the per-directory policy hash tables (`net->xfrm.policy_dird[h]`).

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The only change is the insertion of a single RCU synchronization point within the `xfrm_policy_fini()` function.
- This `synchronize_rcu()` is placed strategically after flushing all policies and before destroying the RCU-protected hash tables (`policy_bydst`).  
- The addition ensures that any RCU readers that may have obtained references to the policy tables via `rcu_dereference_check()` complete their read-side critical sections before the memory is freed.  
- The fix directly addresses the race condition described in the commit message: netns teardown was previously freeing the hash tables without waiting for concurrent RCU readers, which could lead to use-after-free errors.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
<text>xfrm_hash_free(rcu_dereference_protected(htab->table, true), sz);</text>
<text>xfrm_hash_free(net->xfrm.policy_byidx, sz);</text>
Reason:
These statements free the RCU-protected hash tables (policy_bydst and policy_byidx) without first waiting for concurrent RCU readers to finish their read-side critical sections, causing a use-after-free race condition.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
<text>synchronize_rcu();</text>
Reason:
This statement ensures that all RCU readers that were accessing the hash tables before the frees have completed, preventing use-after-free when the tables are subsequently freed.
